rationale: Neuronpedia's sparse-autoencoder feature browser and attribution-graph/circuit tracer are a direct, hosted implementation of mechanistic analysis of model internals (activations, learned features) across many open models -- exactly RQ21's question about using internals-based analysis to understand a model's capabilities and weaknesses, and how generalisable such methods are across models.

Granite Guardian's judge models classify a given prompt/response/context against safety-risk categories (jailbreak, bias, violence, hallucination) and return a pass/fail-style assessment, directly implementing RQ55's context-query-response risk assessment for safety-requirement compliance -- the same guardrail-classifier pattern as guardrailsai/nemo-guardrails/pku-beaver already mapped here.

MExGen and CELL require full white-box access to the model (to compute perturbation and contrastive attributions), producing exactly the kind of local explainability evidence needed to verify model properties with full access -- the same role AI Explainability 360 already plays for RQ54.

Token Highlighter uses gradient-based critical-token identification specifically to detect jailbreak-triggering tokens, a concrete method for improving the robustness of adversarial-attack detection, which is exactly RQ86's question.
